title: General Dihedral-Galois Criterion for X^n - a (dihedral recognition engine)

problemStatement.formal: Provide the reusable group-theoretic core of the general dihedral binomial problem: a constructor building `G ≃* DihedralGroup n` from a generating pair `(σ, τ)` satisfying `σ^n = 1`, `τ^2 = 1`, `τστ⁻¹ = σ⁻¹` together with `|G| = 2n`.
problemStatement.plain: Fill the Mathlib gap flagged by the parent oq-03: there is no `DihedralGroup.lift`. Build the presentation-by-generators-and-relations lift plus the recognition theorem identifying any suitably-generated order-2n group as D_n.
whyMatters: The parent oq-03 discharged only the n=4 case, and did so by a Sylow argument special to |S_4| = 24. A general-n dihedral criterion needs an n-uniform recognition tool.
The S4 PREP Mathlib audit (oq-03 tracker) identified `DihedralGroup.lift` as ABSENT from Mathlib v4.26.0 and a recurring need in classical Galois formalisations.
The recognition theorem is Capelli-free: it is pure group theory, so it is provable now even though the full Schinzel-Velez criterion remains blocked on Capelli's irreducibility theorem upstream.

proven: DihedralGroup n is presented by ⟨s, t | s^n = t^2 = (st)^2 = 1⟩ (equivalently tst⁻¹ = s⁻¹); Mathlib provides the group and its multiplication table but not the lift out of it.
Any finite group with a cyclic subgroup of index 2 acting by inversion is metacyclic; the dihedral case is the sub-case where the acting involution inverts the whole rotation subgroup.
open: Full Schinzel-Velez decidable criterion for arbitrary (n, a) — blocked upstream on Capelli's irreducibility theorem (not in Mathlib v4.26.0).
Concrete generator exhibition σ, τ for Gal(X^n − a) in the dihedral cases (n ∈ {3,4,6,8,12}-type), which would feed directly into the recognition theorem.
knownResults.goal: Deliver `liftHom` (DihedralGroup n →* G from the relations) and `nonempty_mulEquiv_dihedralGroup` (recognition of order-2n generated groups as D_n), verified with 0 sorries / 0 axioms.

knowledge.progressSummary: ACT (researcher-5, 2026-07-02): Created `proofs/Proofs/InverseGaloisD4OQ03Incomplete01.lean` filling the `DihedralGroup.lift` gap. Contents: (1) periodicity/rotation helpers `pow_mod`, `spow_add`, `spow_neg` making i ↦ σ^i.val an additive ZMod n → G map; (2) reflection commutation `sigma_pow_mul_tau : σ^m·τ = τ·(σ^m)⁻¹` by induction from τσ = σ⁻¹τ; (3) combination laws `rot_mul_refl`, `refl_mul_refl`; (4) `liftHom : DihedralGroup n →* G` with the homomorphism law proved from the relations (NOT decide — works for arbitrary carrier G); (5) recognition theorem `nonempty_mulEquiv_dihedralGroup`: σ,τ generating with the relations and |G| = 2n (n ≥ 2) ⟹ G ≃* DihedralGroup n, via surjectivity of liftHom on generators + Fintype.bijective_iff_surjective_and_card. 0 sorries, 0 axioms, 0 native_decide.

Supporting lemmas pow_mod, spow_add, spow_neg, sigma_pow_mul_tau, rot_mul_refl, refl_mul_refl, liftHom_r_one, liftHom_sr_zero — all VERIFIED. Gallery page src/data/proofs/inverse-galois-d4-oq-03-incomplete-01/ (meta.json + annotations.json) created.
insights: The parent's Sylow route (order-8 subgroup of S_4 is D_4) does not generalise; the generators-and-relations route does. The reusable core is `DihedralGroup.lift` — build the hom OUT of DihedralGroup n by pattern matching (r i ↦ σ^i.val, sr i ↦ τσ^i.val) and prove map_mul from the relations, then upgrade to MulEquiv by matching orders (surjective + equal finite card ⟹ bijective).

Proving the hom law for an arbitrary carrier G (not S_4) requires the ZMod-periodicity lemma σ^(k%n) = σ^k (from σ^n = 1) plus the single commutation identity σ^m·τ = τ·(σ^m)⁻¹; every one of the four DihedralGroup multiplication cases (r·r, r·sr, sr·r, sr·sr) reduces to these two facts.

For recognition (not just a hom), the cheap sufficient hypotheses are: generation (closure {σ,τ} = ⊤, giving surjectivity since liftHom hits σ = liftHom(r 1) and τ = liftHom(sr 0)) plus |G| = 2n = |DihedralGroup n| (giving injectivity for free via Fintype.bijective_iff_surjective_and_card). No need to verify injectivity by hand.
mathlibGaps: `DihedralGroup.lift` (presentation-by-generators-and-relations constructor) — this file supplies a self-contained version; a polished form is upstream-contributable.
Capelli's full irreducibility theorem (still absent; blocks the general (n,a) criterion).
nextSteps: Exhibit explicit generators σ, τ for a second concrete dihedral binomial case (e.g. Gal(X^3 − 2) ≅ S_3 ≅ D_3) and feed them to `nonempty_mulEquiv_dihedralGroup` to obtain a non-n=4 dihedral realization.
Consider polishing `liftHom` / `nonempty_mulEquiv_dihedralGroup` into a Mathlib PR adding `DihedralGroup.lift`.
Re-derive the parent's (4,2) case through the recognition theorem (alternative to Sylow) once explicit generators of Gal(X^4 − 2) are named.
